q: Pablo Antonio's early works include buildings for which three institutions?
o: UP, the Metropolitan Theater, and the Post Office
Ateneo, Meralco, and San Miguel Corporation
Far Eastern University, the Philippine National Bank, and the Manila Railroad Company
UST, the Central Bank, and the Manila Hotel
n: Antonio designed for FEU, the PNB, and the Manila Railroad Company. FEU became his signature campus, with its Art Deco Nicanor Reyes Hall.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Antonio, Pablo Sebrero

q: The Philippine National Bank building on Escolta is credited to which designer of the Philamlife Building?
n: Carlos Arguelles, who designed the Philamlife Building and the Manila Hilton, is credited with PNB Escolta. The PNB, founded in 1916, kept its head office on Escolta when that street was Manila's business centre.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arguelles, Carlos D.; Calma

q: For the Development Bank of the Philippines building in Makati, who designed the building and who did its interiors?
o: Lorenzo Calma, with interiors by Carlos Arguelles
Gabriel Formoso, with interiors by Edith Oliveros
Felipe Mendoza, with interiors by Ched Berenguer-Topacio
Carlos Arguelles, with interiors by Lorenzo Calma
n: Carlos Arguelles designed the DBP building, and Lorenzo Calma did its interiors. The DBP, a state development bank, was established in 1958 as the successor of the Rehabilitation Finance Corporation.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arguelles, Carlos D.; Calma, Lorenzo Licad

q: Which architect of Tutuban Station is credited with the Heacock Store Building?
n: Juan Hervas, who designed Tutuban Station and the Arranque and Herran markets, is credited with the Heacock Store Building. Tomas Arguelles is credited with Heacock's Building on Escolta.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Hervas, Juan

q: Besides Otilio Arellano, which architect of the Batasang Pambansa is also credited with the RCBC building on Buendia?
n: Felipe Mendoza is also credited with the RCBC Buendia building. Both architects were UAP presidents, Mendoza in 1979–1980 and Arellano in 1981.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 20–21 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Otilio; Mendoza, Felipe

q: Which architect of the Silahis Hotel and Puerto Azul Resort is also credited with the Development Academy of the Philippines in Tagaytay City?
n: Lorenzo Calma is credited with DAP Tagaytay, a project also attributed to Gabriel Formoso.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Calma, Lorenzo Licad; Formoso

q: The Development Academy of the Philippines building in Pasig was designed by whom?
n: Felipe Mendoza designed the DAP building in Pasig. The DAP itself was created in 1973 by Presidential Decree 205 as the government's training and research institution.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mendoza, Felipe Marcelo

q: Besides Carlos Arguelles, which hotel and resort architect is credited with the PNB building on Escolta?
n: Lorenzo Calma is also credited with PNB Escolta, alongside Carlos Arguelles.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Calma, Lorenzo Licad; Arguelles, Carlos D.

q: Heacock's Building on Escolta is credited to which architect of the Elizalde Building?
n: Tomas Arguelles, who designed the Elizalde Building on Muelle de la Industria, is credited with Heacock's Building. H.E. Heacock was one of Escolta's leading department stores before World War II.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arguelles, Tomas Fernandez

q: The Development Academy of the Philippines complex in Tagaytay City is credited to which designer of the Central Bank complex?
n: Gabriel Formoso, architect of the Central Bank complex, is credited with DAP Tagaytay. Lorenzo Calma is also credited with that project. The DAP building in Pasig is a separate work, by Felipe Mendoza.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Formoso; Calma

q: The Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation (RCBC) building on Buendia Avenue, Makati is credited to which of these architects?
n: Otilio Arellano is credited with the RCBC building on Buendia. Records also credit Felipe Mendoza with the same building, so either name may be the one you meet in an exam.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 20–21 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Otilio; Mendoza, Felipe

q: Johnny Hubilla is known for designing what?
o: Philippine trade houses and pavilions abroad, in Bangkok, Toronto, Mainz, Leipzig, and Spokane
n: Hubilla designed Philippine trade houses and exposition pavilions overseas, including the pavilion at the 1974 Spokane World's Fair.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Hubilla, Johnny

q: The FEU Hospital, the Mormon Temple at Green Meadows, and San Jose Seminary at Ateneo de Manila share which architect?
n: All three are Felipe Mendoza's. Pablo Antonio designed FEU's main campus buildings, not the hospital.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mendoza, Felipe Marcelo

q: Which of these is NOT a William Coscolluela work?
o: Shoemart City, Cebu and Quezon City
n: Rockwell Center is Felino Palafox Jr.'s. Robinson's Pasig, the Atrium, Galeria de Magallanes, Shoemart City, and the Magellan Hotel in Cebu are Coscolluela's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Coscolluela; Palafox

q: Which corporate headquarters in Mandaluyong is credited to the Mañosa Brothers, and also to Jose Mañosa?
n: The SMC Head Office on Ortigas Avenue is a Mañosa Brothers work, with Jose Mañosa credited. Its terraced green façade reflects their tropical design approach.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa Brothers; Mañosa, Jose

q: Froilan Bautista Hong designed which Pasay landmark, built in the early 1980s at the CCP Complex?
n: Hong designed the Manila Film Center (1982), modelled on the Parthenon. The Folk Arts Theater and PICC are Locsin's, and the Coconut Palace is Francisco Mañosa's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Hong, Froilan Bautista

q: Which architect designed the Batasang Pambansa Buildings in Quezon City, seat of the House of Representatives?
n: Felipe Marcelo Mendoza designed the Batasang Pambansa complex, built in the late 1970s. He also served as UAP president in 1979–1980.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mendoza, Felipe Marcelo

q: Sierra Lake Resorts, Hidden Valley Springs Resort, Maya-maya Resort, and the Makiling Conference Center were designed by whom?
n: These resort and retreat projects are by the Mañosa Brothers, who drew on native materials and forms.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa Brothers

q: The Wack-Wack Twin Towers, Quezon City Sports Club, and the Centro Escolar University complex in Malolos were designed by whom?
n: William Vargas Coscolluela designed all three; his firm shaped much of Metro Manila's commercial skyline in the 1980s–90s.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Coscolluela, William Vargas

q: Museo Iloilo, Tinucuan Chapel in Passi, Barbaza Church in Antique, and plaza plans for Molo, Jaro, and La Paz were designed by whom?
n: Sergio Villar Penasales worked mainly in Panay, designing Museo Iloilo and the town plaza master plans for Iloilo City's districts.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Penasales, Sergio Villar

q: Interiors of the Admiral Hotel, Cebu Plaza Hotel, and the Philippine Houses in Chicago and Houston, plus Alaala Park in Pagsanjan, are works of whom?
n: Edith L. Oliveros designed those interiors and park projects.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Oliveros, Edith L.

q: Besides the SMC Head Office, Jose Tronqued Mañosa designed which bank headquarters?
n: Jose Mañosa designed the BPI Head Office in Makati.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa, Jose Tronqued

q: Which of these is NOT a work of the Mañosa Brothers?
n: The Manila Film Center is Froilan Hong's. The Mañosa Brothers did Colegio de San Agustin, Andres Soriano Memorial Hospital, the Sulo Restaurant, Bislig Bay Lumber, and the Guadalupe restoration.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 20–21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa Brothers; Hong

q: Ched Berenguer-Topacio is recognised for which kind of design work?
n: Berenguer-Topacio is known as an interior designer for hotels, restaurants, and similar spaces.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Berenguer-Topacio, Ched

q: Rockwell Center, the Rizal Tower, and Luna Gardens are works of which architect-planner?
n: Felino Palafox Jr., known for urban planning and master-planned developments, designed these projects at Rockwell.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Palafox, Felino Jr.

q: Which Filipino designer's interior work includes the Palace Hotel in Beijing and buildings in Abu Dhabi such as the National Bank and Arab Monetary Fund?
n: Edgardo P. Ramirez designed those interiors abroad, along with interiors for a Philippine Embassy.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Ramirez, Edgardo P.

q: The Silahis Hotel on Roxas Boulevard, the Midtown Ramada Hotel, Puerto Azul Resort in Ternate, and Benguet Center were designed by whom?
n: Lorenzo Licad Calma designed these hotels and resorts.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Calma, Lorenzo Licad

q: The PCIB (Antonino) Building on Kalaw Street and the Xavier University library in Cagayan de Oro were designed by whom?
n: Both are by Felipe Mendoza, whose list also includes Assumption School buildings in Antipolo.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mendoza, Felipe Marcelo

q: The Palacio del Gobernador in Intramuros, rebuilt in the 1970s, is the work of which architect?
n: Otilio Arellano designed the modern Palacio del Gobernador. He is a different, later architect from the brothers Juan and Arcadio Arellano.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Otilio A.

q: Otilio A. Arellano designed which government building on Taft Avenue?
o: The National Bureau of Investigation building
n: Otilio Arellano designed the NBI Building on Taft Avenue, as well as the Palacio del Gobernador in Intramuros.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Otilio A.

q: Industrial plants for Dole in Polomolok, Standard Vacuum in Limay, General Milling in Mactan, and Republic Cement in Norzagaray were designed by whom?
n: Alfredo Luz designed these plants, along with the Far East Bank head office in Intramuros.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Luz, Alfredo J. Dimayuga

q: Cresenciano Cruz de Castro designed campus buildings for which two state universities?
o: UP Diliman and UP Los Baños
Mindanao State University (Marawi) and Central Luzon State University (Muñoz)
n: De Castro designed buildings at MSU in Marawi and CLSU in Muñoz, Nueva Ecija.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: De Castro, Cresenciano Cruz

q: The Atomic Research Center in Quezon City and the National Science Development Board complex in Taguig were designed by whom?
n: Both science facilities are de Castro's, as are projects for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: De Castro, Cresenciano Cruz

q: The Times Theater on Quezon Boulevard, Manila Doctors' Hospital, and Makati Medical Center were designed by whom?
n: Luis Maria Gonzaga Araneta designed all three. Mendoza's hospital is the FEU Hospital.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Araneta, Luis Maria Gonzaga

q: Palma Hall and Melchor Hall at UP Diliman were designed by whom?
n: Cesar Homero Concio designed Palma Hall (AS Building) and Melchor Hall (Engineering), plus UP's Protestant Chapel, the Church of the Risen Lord. Nakpil did UP's administration and library buildings.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Concio, Cesar Homero

q: The Central Bank complex and the Metropolitan Museum of Manila were designed by which architect?
n: Gabriel Papa Formoso designed the Central Bank (now BSP) complex on Roxas Boulevard, which houses the Metropolitan Museum.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Formoso, Gabriel Papa

q: Sining Kayumanggi at Mehan Gardens and the Philippine School of Business Administration on Aurora Boulevard were designed by whom?
n: Both are Otilio Arellano's. He also served as UAP president in 1981.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Otilio A.

q: Alejandro Yelab Caudal is best known for which type of work?
o: Private residences, such as the Jacinto, Lopa, Lerma, and Tiongco houses
n: Caudal's works are residences: the Jacinto Residence in Bustos, the Luis Santos House in Malolos, the Lopa Residence in Pasay, the Lerma House, and the Tiongco House in Pandacan.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Caudal, Alejandro Yelab

q: Alfredo J. Luz designed the headquarters of which international organisation in Manila?
n: Luz designed the WHO Western Pacific Regional Headquarters on Taft Avenue, the Ramon Magsaysay Building, and IRRI in Los Baños. The ADB's old office is linked to de Castro.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Luz, Alfredo J. Dimayuga

q: The Philamlife Building and the Manila Hilton (now Manila Pavilion) on United Nations Avenue were designed by whom?
n: Carlos D. Arguelles designed both; the Philamlife Building (1961) was noted for its modernist auditorium. Tomas Arguelles is an earlier architect known for the Elizalde Building.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arguelles, Carlos D.

q: Holiday Inn on Roxas Boulevard, Urdaneta and Tuscany Apartments, and the Chronicle Broadcasting Network Studios are works of which architect?
n: All are by Carlos Arguelles. Calma's hotels include the Silahis and Midtown Ramada.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arguelles, Carlos D.

q: Which Paranaque church did Cesar Concio design?
o: Baclaran Church, the National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help
n: Concio designed Baclaran's Modern Romanesque church (1953–1958), which seats 2,000 and has stayed open 24 hours since opening. He also did the Union Church of Manila.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Concio, Cesar Homero

q: The National Press Club Building, the former PLDT head office in Makati, and the Lopez Museum were designed by whom?
n: These are Angel E. Nakpil's. Juan Nakpil, the National Artist, is known for Quiapo Church and UP buildings.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Angel E. Sancho

q: Santa Catalina College on Legarda and the Botica Boie Building on Escolta share which architect?
n: Both are by Luis Araneta. Botica Boie was one of Escolta's best-known pharmacies.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Araneta, Luis Maria Gonzaga

q: The Asian Institute of Management, Club Filipino, Valley Golf Club, and Alabang Golf and Country Club share which architect?
n: All four are Formoso's; Club Filipino in Greenhills is where Corazon Aquino took her oath in 1986.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Formoso, Gabriel Papa

q: The Picache Building in Quiapo, the Roche Building on Pasong Tamo, and Petrona Apartments on Taft Avenue are works of which architect?
n: All three are Angel Nakpil's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Angel E. Sancho

q: Which of these is NOT a Cesar Concio work?
o: UP College of Forestry, Los Baños
n: Makati Medical Center is Luis Araneta's. Concio designed the Children's Memorial Hospital, the Insular Life Building, the UP College of Forestry, and Silliman University buildings.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Concio; Araneta

q: Which research institute in Los Baños was designed by Alfredo Luz?
n: IRRI's campus is Luz's. The UP College of Forestry is Concio's and the National Arts Center is Locsin's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Luz, Alfredo J. Dimayuga

q: Which architect of the Batasang Pambansa served as UAP president from 1979 to 1980?
n: Felipe M. Mendoza, who designed the Batasang Pambansa buildings, led the UAP in 1979–1980, after Ruperto C. Gaite (1977–1978).
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: In December 2005, the UAP was a Regional Nominee in which search, run by the Philippine National Volunteer Service Coordinating Agency?
n: The PNVSCA nominated the UAP in its 'Search for Outstanding Volunteers' for work on housing, urban degradation, and conservation, during National Volunteer Month.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Who was the charter president of the United Architects of the Philippines (1975)?
n: Norberto M. Nuke was charter president in 1975. Jose V. Herrera followed as the first regular president in 1976.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: The architect of the Manila Film Center served as UAP president during which years?
n: Froilan L. Hong, designer of the Manila Film Center, was UAP president in 1987–1988, after Cesar V. Canchela (1985–1986).
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: The UAP's first international award, received in Adelaide, Australia in November 2010, was what?
n: EAROPH, the Eastern Regional Organization for Planning and Human Settlements, gave the UAP its 50th Golden Jubilee Award for contributions to planning and human settlements.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Who was the first woman to serve as UAP national president (1998–2000)?
n: Yolanda D. Reyes (1998–2000) was the first woman to lead the UAP. Prosperidad C. Luis succeeded her, and Ana Ling and Benita Regala served later.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: Who became UAP president in 2018?
n: Benjamin K. Panganiban Jr. took office in 2018, succeeding Guillermo H. Hisancha (2016–2018).
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: Which National Artist for Architecture served as UAP president in 1981–1982?
n: Leandro V. Locsin, designer of the CCP and PICC, led the UAP in 1981–1982. Manuel T. Mañosa followed in 1983–1984.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: How many times has the UAP won the PRC's Most Outstanding Accredited Professional Organization award, making it the first and only APO to do so?
n: The UAP won it four times, in 2002, 2007, 2008, and 2011, besting 42 other organisations under 12 criteria.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Who served as the first regular president of the UAP in 1976, after the charter presidency?
n: Jose V. Herrera is president no. 1 (1976), following charter president Norberto Nuke.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — UAP Presidents

q: In April 2009, the UAP's Green Architecture Movement received which environmental award?
o: The Father Neri Satur Award for Environmental Heroism
n: It won the Father Neri Satur Award for Environmental Heroism, named after a priest killed defending forests; the UAP was the only accredited professional organisation to receive it.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: In which years did the UAP win the PRC's Most Outstanding Accredited Professional Organization award?
n: The winning years were 2002, 2007, 2008, and 2011.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Which of these women did NOT serve as UAP president?
n: Edith L. Oliveros is known for interiors and park designs, not the UAP presidency. Luis, Ling, and Regala all led the UAP.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 19 and 21 — UAP Presidents; Filipino Architects

q: Why was the AIAAF dissolved in 1911?
o: The civil engineers withdrew to form their own organisation
n: The civil engineers left to form their own body, ending the joint academy after its failed struggle to pass an Engineers and Architects Law.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Who is recorded as the first Filipino architect?
n: Félix Roxas y Arroyo, born about 1820 in Manila, studied in Spain and worked for years in England and France before practising at home. The Arellanos and Nakpil belong to the 20th century.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: The country's earliest architecture school was opened by the AIAAF in 1904. Name it and give the length of its courses.
o: Mapúa Institute of Technology; four years
UST College of Architecture; six years
Escuela de Ingeniería y Arquitectura; five years
n: The Escuela de Ingeniería y Arquitectura offered five-year courses in architecture and civil engineering. Mapúa was founded later, in 1925.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Architecture first received its own separate statute on 17 June 1950. Which law was it?
n: RA 545, 'An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines', took effect 17 June 1950. RA 9266 replaced it in 2004 as the Architecture Act.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Before formal architecture schooling existed, how did a Filipino typically learn to design and build?
o: By apprenticing under a maestro de obras, or master builder
By joining the colonial army engineers
By enrolling in the Escuela de Ingeniería y Arquitectura
n: The maestro de obras trained builders on the job. A formal school for master builders opened only in the 1890s, and the Escuela de Ingeniería y Arquitectura came later, in 1904.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: During the Spanish colonial period, how many schools of architecture existed in the Philippines?
o: One, attached to the University of Santo Tomas
n: There were no architecture schools under Spain. Would-be architects either trained abroad, like Félix Roxas in Spain, or learned under a maestro de obras.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: The Academia de Arquitectura y Agrimensura de Filipinas maintained direct consultation with which foreign body?
o: The Royal Institute of British Architects
The Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
n: Under American rule, the AAAF consulted directly with the American Institute of Architects (AIA).
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Which 1921 law was the first enabling law for the practice of engineering and architecture, defining them as separate professions?
n: Act No. 2985, passed by the Philippine Legislature in 1921, first defined engineering and architecture as distinct professions. RA 545 (1950) later gave architecture its own law.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: On 14 September 1902, engineers, surveyors, and graduates of the master-builders' school founded the first professional body of architects. What was it called?
o: Academia de Arquitectura y Agrimensura de Filipinas (AAAF)
n: The AAAF was the first professional organisation of architects and allied professionals. The PIA and LPA came decades later and merged into the UAP in 1974.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: A year after its founding, the AAAF changed its name to include which additional profession?
o: Engineering, becoming the Academia de Ingeniería, Arquitectura y Agrimensura de Filipinas
Planning, becoming the Academia de Urbanismo
Fine arts, becoming the Academia de Bellas Artes
Law, becoming the Academia de Derecho y Arquitectura
n: The body became the AIAAF by adding 'Ingeniería', formally bringing engineers into the organisation alongside architects and surveyors.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: Which university's Art Deco campus buildings, including its administration and science buildings, are famous works of Pablo Antonio?
n: Pablo Antonio designed the FEU campus, whose Nicanor Reyes Hall is a celebrated Art Deco landmark. UP Diliman's Palma and Melchor Halls are by Cesar Concio.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Antonio, Pablo Sebrero

q: Which public infrastructure did Francisco Mañosa design, giving it a Filipino vernacular look?
n: Mañosa designed LRT Line 1 stations with roofs drawn from the bahay kubo. He also did the Mary Immaculate Parish Church and Moonwalk Subdivision in Las Piñas. NAIA is Locsin's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa, Francisco Tronqued

q: The Makati Stock Exchange Building, the Ayala Museum, and the National Arts Center in Laguna share which architect?
n: All three are Locsin's; the National Arts Center on Mt. Makiling houses the Philippine High School for the Arts.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Locsin, Leandro V.

q: Which hotel project is NOT credited to Leandro Locsin?
n: The Manila Peninsula is by Gabriel Formoso. Locsin designed the Philippine Plaza, the Hyatt Regency, and the Mandarin Oriental, and renovated the Manila Hotel.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 20–21 — Filipino Architects: Locsin; Formoso

q: Which national shrine did Juan Nakpil reconstruct?
o: The Rizal House in Calamba, Laguna
n: Nakpil rebuilt José Rizal's birthplace in Calamba, destroyed in World War II, using period research to recreate the bahay na bato.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Juan Felipe de Jesus

q: Francisco T. Mañosa, National Artist for Architecture in 2018, designed Tahanang Pilipino at the CCP Complex. By what popular name is it known?
n: Tahanang Pilipino (1978) is the Coconut Palace, built largely of coconut materials as a showcase of Filipino design.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa, Francisco Tronqued

q: Which of these is NOT a work of Pablo Antonio?
n: The Metropolitan Theater (1931) is by Juan Arellano. The preventorium, the Roces building, and the Roxas Boulevard apartments are Antonio's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Antonio; Arellano, Juan

q: Which restoration and development projects are credited to Francisco Mañosa?
o: Las Piñas Church, Quezon Memorial Circle, and Corregidor Island
n: Mañosa restored the Las Piñas (Bamboo Organ) Church and developed Quezon Memorial Circle and Corregidor. The Rizal House reconstruction is Juan Nakpil's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa, Francisco Tronqued

q: Which of these is NOT by Juan Nakpil?
n: The Philamlife Building on UN Avenue is by Carlos Arguelles. The Quezon Institute, Philippine Trust, Security Bank, and the Gen. Vicente Lim Residence are Nakpil's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 20–21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Juan; Arguelles, Carlos

q: Which UP Diliman buildings are credited to Juan Nakpil?
n: Nakpil designed UP's Administration Building (Quezon Hall) and the University Library (Gonzalez Hall). Palma and Melchor Halls are Concio's; Villamor Hall, at UP Manila, is Juan Arellano's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Juan Felipe de Jesus

q: Leandro V. Locsin was proclaimed National Artist for Architecture in which year?
n: Locsin was proclaimed in 1990, four years before his death. His monumental 'floating volume' concrete style defined the CCP Complex.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Locsin, Leandro V.

q: The Ideal Theater and Galaxy Theater on Rizal Avenue and the Manila Polo Club were designed by whom?
n: All three are Pablo Antonio's; the Ideal Theater (1933) was his major early work. Juan Nakpil's theaters were the Ever and State.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Antonio, Pablo Sebrero

q: The Manila Jockey Club, the Avenue Hotel and Theater, and the Ever and State Theaters are works of which architect?
n: All are by Juan Nakpil, along with the Geronimo de los Reyes and Capitan Pepe Buildings. Angel Nakpil's list includes the National Press Club and the Lopez Museum.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Juan Felipe de Jesus

q: Which two major works outside Metro Manila's CCP Complex show Leandro Locsin's reach, one of them abroad?
o: Manila Film Center and the Coconut Palace
IRRI and the WHO Regional Office
Manila International Airport (NAIA) and the Istana Nurul Iman in Brunei
n: Locsin designed the NAIA terminal and the Istana Nurul Iman, the Sultan of Brunei's palace, one of the largest residential palaces in the world.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Locsin, Leandro V.

q: Pablo S. Antonio, known for Art Deco landmarks in Manila, was named National Artist for Architecture in what year?
n: Pablo Antonio became National Artist in 1976. Juan Nakpil was first, in 1973; Locsin followed in 1990 and Francisco Mañosa in 2018.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Antonio, Pablo Sebrero

q: Which cluster of buildings at the CCP Complex is the work of Leandro Locsin?
o: Tahanang Pilipino and the Film Center
Sofitel Philippine Plaza and Harbour Square
Manila Film Center and Coconut Palace
Main Theater, Folk Arts Theater, PICC, and PHILCITE
n: Locsin designed the CCP Main Theater (1969), the Folk Arts Theater, the Philippine International Convention Center (1976), and PHILCITE. Tahanang Pilipino is Francisco Mañosa's and the Film Center is Froilan Hong's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Locsin, Leandro V.

q: Which shrine on Ortigas Avenue, at EDSA, was designed by Francisco Mañosa?
o: Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help
Shrine of Jesus the Way, the Truth and the Life
Shrine of Our Lady of Manaoag
Shrine of Our Lady of Peace
n: The Shrine of Our Lady of Peace, the EDSA Shrine (1989), commemorates the People Power Revolution. The Perpetual Help shrine in Baclaran is by César Concio.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Mañosa, Francisco Tronqued

q: Juan F. Nakpil, the first National Artist for Architecture (1973), designed which church in Manila?
n: Nakpil rebuilt Quiapo Church in the 1930s and later expanded it. Manila Cathedral's present form is by Fernando Ocampo, and the current Santo Domingo by José Zaragoza.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Nakpil, Juan Felipe de Jesus

q: Which three architects' associations survived into the early 1970s and later united as the UAP?
n: The Association of Philippine Government Architects, the League of Philippine Architects, and the Philippine Institute of Architects merged. The AAAF and AIAAF had dissolved decades earlier.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: When the three associations merged into the UAP, how many members joined automatically, and how many registered for active membership in the first year?
n: All 1,300 members of APGA, LPA, and PIA became UAP members, and 700 officially registered as active in the first year.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: On what date was the United Architects of the Philippines born?
n: The UAP was founded on 12 December 1974. It was then registered with the SEC on 26 March 1975 and accredited by the PRC on 12 May 1975.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: On 22 June 2004 the PRC, through the Board of Architecture, accredited the UAP under what designation?
o: Accredited Professional Organization of the Year
Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
n: Under RA 9266 the UAP became the IAPOA, the single integrated organisation all registered architects belong to.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: In June 1973, which decree created the Professional Regulation Commission, requiring a single accredited organisation per profession?
n: President Marcos issued PD 223 creating the PRC. Its one-organisation rule pushed APGA, LPA, and PIA to unite. PD 1096 is the National Building Code.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: What distinction came with the PRC Certificate No. 001 issued to the UAP on 12 May 1975?
o: It made the UAP the first professional organisation accredited by the PRC
It licensed the UAP to issue building permits
It made the UAP the first Philippine member of the UIA
It made the UAP a government agency
n: Certificate No. 001 marked the UAP as the very first organisation accredited by the Professional Regulation Commission.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: The UAP was instrumental in passing Republic Act 9266, the Architecture Act of 2004. When did it take effect?
n: RA 9266 was signed on 17 March 2004 and took effect on 26 April 2004, replacing RA 545 of 1950.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: What did Republic Act 9266 give Filipino architects?
o: More definite rights, benefits, and distinction compared with other professionals in construction
The power to act as building officials
n: RA 9266 clarified the scope of architectural practice, giving architects clearer rights and distinction from other construction professionals such as engineers.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: On what date was the UAP registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission?
n: SEC registration came on 26 March 1975, when the vision of unifying the three associations formally materialised.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 19 — History of the UAP

q: The Sy Cong Bieng Mausoleum, the San Vicente de Paul Chapel, and the Alfonso Zobel and E.A. Perkins residences share which architect?
n: All are Luna de San Pedro's; his list also includes the Basa and Evangelista residences and work at the North Cemetery.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Luna de San Pedro, Andres

q: Which two neoclassical government buildings are credited to Juan Arellano?
o: The Legislative Building and the Post Office Building
Malacañang Palace and the Army-Navy Club
The Manila Hotel and the Philippine General Hospital
The Central Bank and the Metropolitan Museum
n: Arellano worked on the Legislative Building (later the Senate and now the National Museum of Fine Arts) and the Manila Central Post Office. The Manila Hotel and PGH are William Parsons's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Juan de Guzman

q: Which UST building is credited to Fernando Ocampo?
n: Ocampo designed the UST Central Seminary Building (1933). The UST Main Building is by Fr. Roque Ruaño.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Ocampo, Fernando Hizon

q: Luciano Oliver, who worked on the reconstruction of Manila Cathedral, also partnered with Fray Marcos Anton on which Batangas church?
n: Don Luciano Oliver worked with Fray Marcos Anton on Taal Church (1858–1878), one of the largest churches in Asia. He is also credited with Manila Cathedral reconstruction.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 17 and 21 — Taal Church; Filipino Architects: Oliver, Luciano

q: Daniel Hudson Burnham's proposed grand plan for Manila involved which street pattern?
n: Burnham's 1905 plan laid a gridiron with diagonal avenues radiating from a civic centre, adapting his City Beautiful ideas to Manila.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Burnham, Daniel Hudson

q: Which Laguna landmark is credited to Vicente B. Belloc?
n: Franciscan Fr. Vicente Belloc built the Nagcarlan Underground Cemetery (1845), with a crypt beneath its chapel.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Belloc, Vicente B.

q: The Arranque and Herran markets and the Assumption Convent on Herran Street are works of whom?
n: Juan Hervas designed both markets and the Assumption Convent.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Hervas, Juan

q: Which planning and campus work is credited to Juan Arellano?
o: The master plan of UP Diliman and Villamor Hall at UP Taft
n: Arellano did the UP Diliman master plan, Villamor Hall at UP Taft, and landscaping plans for Padre Burgos Avenue, Harrison Park, Roxas Boulevard, and Malacañang.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Juan de Guzman

q: Fernando Hizon Ocampo designed which cathedral, rebuilt in 1954–1958?
n: Ocampo designed the present Manila Metropolitan Cathedral, built under Cardinal Rufino Santos and completed in 1958.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Ocampo, Fernando Hizon

q: Legarda Elementary School and St. Cecilia's Hall at St. Scholastica's College were designed by which architect?
n: Both are by Andres Luna de San Pedro, one of Manila's leading architects of the 1920s–30s.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Luna de San Pedro, Andres

q: The Estrella del Norte and the Paris-Manila Building, both on Escolta, were designed by which architect?
n: Both commercial buildings are by Juan Hervas.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Hervas, Juan

q: Juan Hervas designed which 19th-century railway terminal?
n: Hervas designed Tutuban Station (1887), the Manila terminus of the Manila–Dagupan railway, now Tutuban Center.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Hervas, Juan

q: Which of these is NOT a work of Fernando Ocampo?
o: Elizalde Building, Muelle de la Industria
n: The Elizalde Building is by Tomas Fernandez Arguelles. The Paterno, Cu Unjieng, Arguelles, and Admiral Apartments buildings and the Oriental Club are Ocampo's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, pp. 20–21 — Filipino Architects: Ocampo; Arguelles, Tomas

q: Andres Luna de San Pedro, son of the painter Juan Luna, designed which Art Deco building on Escolta?
n: Luna de San Pedro designed the Perez-Samanillo Building (now First United Building). Botica Boie is Luis Araneta's and Cu Unjieng is Fernando Ocampo's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Luna de San Pedro, Andres

q: Which friar-architect proposed repairs for the Colegio de Santa Potenciana and oversaw the reconstruction of Manila Cathedral?
n: Juan de Uguccioni, a Florentine friar, oversaw the cathedral work and added its media naranja dome in 1750.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: De Uguccioni, Juan

q: Roman Ongpin's bazaar 'El 82', Hotel de Francia, and the Casino Español on Taft Avenue were designed by whom?
n: Arcadio de Guzman Arellano, elder brother of Juan Arellano, designed these turn-of-the-century buildings.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Arcadio de Guzman

q: Who implemented Burnham's plans for Baguio and Manila and prepared city plans for Cebu and Zamboanga?
n: William E. Parsons, consulting architect of the Philippine government (1905–1914), carried out Burnham's plans and designed landmarks like the Manila Hotel and PGH.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 21 — Filipino Architects: Parsons, William E.

q: Juan de Guzman Arellano designed which Art Deco landmark in Manila (1931)?
n: Juan Arellano's Manila Metropolitan Theater is a major Art Deco landmark. The Ideal Theater is Pablo Antonio's and the Times Theater is Luis Araneta's.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Juan de Guzman

q: The Carmelo and Bauermann Building in Azcarraga and the Gota de Leche Building on S.H. Loyola were designed by which architect?
n: Both are by Arcadio Arellano. Gota de Leche, a charity milk station for infants, is now a heritage building.
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 20 — Filipino Architects: Arellano, Arcadio de Guzman
